description: CanDo sample point-factor job evaluation plan. Original to CanDo; a starting point a tenant copies, reviews with its pay equity committee or advisers, adjusts and publishes as its own plan version (docs/19 §5). Covers the four groups that Canadian pay equity laws compare: skill, effort, responsibility and working conditions.
points_rule: Each factor's degrees step evenly from step to max_points (degree n = n x step). The table holds the points; the rule is only how they were set.

factors.definition_en: The knowledge the job needs to be done at a fully competent level, however it is gained: schooling, training, apprenticeship or equivalent experience. Rate the job, not the incumbent's credentials.

degrees.descriptor_en: Basic reading, writing and arithmetic; follows simple written and spoken instructions.
Secondary school or equivalent; knowledge of standard procedures for the work.
Secondary school plus several months of job-specific training, a short certificate, or equivalent on-the-job learning.
A one-year college program, an apprenticeship of under two years, or equivalent specialized knowledge.
A two- or three-year college diploma, a completed apprenticeship, or equivalent specialized knowledge of a field.
A bachelor's degree or equivalent professional knowledge of a discipline.
Advanced knowledge of a discipline: a master's degree, a professional designation with advanced practice, or equivalent.
Expert knowledge of a field or of several disciplines, recognized beyond the organization.

evidence.note_en: From the job's NOC code (docs/18). TEER describes the usual education and training of the occupation; the job's own requirements (docs/18 §6) may be higher or lower.

factors.definition_en: The practical experience needed, beyond the knowledge in K1, before a person can do the job at a fully competent level. Count experience that can be gained in paid or unpaid work.

degrees.descriptor_en: Up to 6 months.
More than 6 months, up to 2 years.
More than 2 years, up to 4 years.
More than 4 years, up to 7 years.
More than 7 years.

factors.definition_en: The skill to exchange information, listen, explain, reassure, persuade, negotiate or teach, including in another language or across cultures.

degrees.descriptor_en: Exchanges routine information courteously.
Explains procedures and gathers information; uses tact with upset people, following set approaches.
Explains complex information to people with different needs; builds trust with people in difficult circumstances; resolves disagreements.
Counsels, persuades, mediates or negotiates where positions differ and the outcome matters; teaches or facilitates groups.
Negotiates or advocates on major issues with senior external parties, or works through highly sensitive, conflicted situations.

factors.definition_en: The concentration, judgement and problem solving the work demands: how complex the problems are, how long attention must be held, and how often work is interrupted or done against competing deadlines.

degrees.descriptor_en: Routine tasks; short periods of attention; problems with obvious answers.
Chooses among set procedures; regular attention to detail; some interruptions.
Analyses varied information to solve problems; sustained concentration; frequent interruptions or competing deadlines.
Complex analysis with few precedents; intense concentration for long periods; many demands handled at once.
New, many-sided problems with high uncertainty; intense concentration under constant competing demands.

factors.definition_en: Physical demands: lifting, carrying, moving or transferring people or objects, standing, walking, awkward positions, and repetitive or fine motor work such as keyboarding or precise hand work.

degrees.descriptor_en: Mostly seated with freedom to move; light objects only.
Regular standing or walking, sustained repetitive fine motor work, or occasional lifting of moderate weights.
Frequent lifting or moving of moderate weights, helping people move, or long periods in fixed positions.
Frequent heavy lifting, transferring people, or strenuous work for much of the day.
Continuous strenuous work, or heavy work in awkward positions.

factors.definition_en: The effort to manage one's own emotions while responding to other people's distress, anger, grief or trauma, or while giving unwelcome news. Rate the demand of the work itself; exposure to a hostile setting is rated in W2.

degrees.descriptor_en: Emotionally demanding contact is rare.
Occasional contact with upset or frustrated people.
Regular contact with people in distress or crisis, or regularly giving unwelcome decisions.
Frequent work with people living through trauma, grief, violence or severe mental health crises.
Intense distress or trauma is the core of the work, every day, such as end-of-life, crisis line or child protection work.

factors.definition_en: The freedom to make decisions and the effect of those decisions and of errors on people served, services, finances and the organization's standing.

degrees.descriptor_en: Follows instructions; errors are found quickly and have little effect.
Decides how to do own tasks within procedures; errors affect own work or one person and are easily corrected.
Decides on cases or tasks within policy; errors could affect several people or a service and take effort to correct.
Decides on a program or significant cases and interprets policy; decisions affect a program or many people.
Sets direction for a department or major function; decisions affect the organization's services or reputation.
Sets organization-wide strategy; decisions affect the whole organization and its standing.

factors.definition_en: Responsibility for the work and development of others: training, directing, supervising and managing employees, volunteers or students.

degrees.descriptor_en: No responsibility for others beyond helping colleagues.
Trains or orients others, or directs volunteers or students on tasks.
Leads others' daily work as a lead hand or coordinator, or supervises a small team.
Manages a team or several supervisors, accountable for hiring, performance and pay recommendations.
Leads a department or the organization through managers.

evidence.also: Direct and indirect reports from the position tree (docs/03) are shown beside the suggestion.

factors.name_en: Responsibility for the wellbeing of others
factors.name_fr: Responsabilité à l’égard du bien-être d’autrui
factors.definition_en: Responsibility for the safety, health, rights or wellbeing of clients, residents, patients, children, participants or the public, including care, protection and advocacy.

degrees.descriptor_en: Limited contact; courtesy and referral.
Gives information or practical help that affects people's access to services.
Gives direct care, support or service where errors could affect a person's wellbeing; follows safety plans.
Assesses risk and makes care, safety or service plans for vulnerable people; acts in emergencies.
Accountable for the safety and wellbeing of many vulnerable people, or for protective decisions with lasting effect.

factors.name_fr: Responsabilité à l’égard des ressources et de l’information
factors.definition_en: Responsibility for money, assets, equipment, facilities and confidential information.

degrees.descriptor_en: Care of own equipment and materials; routine, non-confidential information.
Handles cash or small purchases, or regularly handles personal information under procedures.
Controls a budget line, inventory or equipment of significant value, or keeps confidential records.
Manages a program budget or major assets, or is accountable for highly sensitive information such as health, legal, pay or personnel records.
Accountable for the organization's finances, assets or information governance.

factors.definition_en: Exposure to unpleasant or hazardous conditions: weather, noise, dirt, odours, chemicals, bodily fluids, infection risk, travel and lone or isolated work.

degrees.descriptor_en: Normal office or similar setting.
Occasional unpleasant conditions, or regular local travel.
Regular unpleasant conditions, infection risk or bodily fluids, or regular work in people's homes or the community.
Frequent hazards that need protective equipment or protocols, or lone work in uncontrolled settings.
Constant exposure to significant hazards.

factors.definition_en: Exposure to verbal abuse, aggression, threats, unpredictable situations and distressing material. The effort of managing one's own emotions is rated in E3.

degrees.descriptor_en: Rare.
Occasional verbal aggression or upsetting material.
Regular verbal aggression, unpredictable situations or distressing material.
Frequent threats or risk of physical aggression; regular exposure to traumatic material.
Constant risk of violence or exposure to traumatic events.

gender_neutral_checks: All four groups (skill, effort, responsibility, working conditions) are present and every job is rated on every factor.
Knowledge is rated as needed by the job however gained, so skills learned through experience, caregiving or community work count.

Factors cover demands common in female-predominant work that older plans missed: emotional effort, responsibility for others' wellbeing, communication and relationship skill, fine motor and repetitive work, interruptions and competing demands, confidential information, and exposure to bodily fluids.
Descriptors use work content, not job titles or gendered examples.
Before publishing, the committee pilots the plan on female- and male-predominant job classes and reviews whether factor weights favour one group.
Each rating records a rationale; ratings outside the evidence-based suggestion record why.
french: Group and factor names are in French. Definitions and degree descriptors need French versions before a French-language plan is published.
